property_summary: For any deployment and inputs, the contract's owner() getter always returns the stored owner address (the owner set by __Ownable_init), whereas the mutant returns address(0) for some inputs thereby violating that stored-owner equality property.
For any initializer caller address A used to initialize C, C.owner() must equal A (the stored owner); the mutant that returns address(0) breaks this when initialized by a non-zero deployer.

For any nonzero initializer address that calls initialize on C, the public owner() getter must return that initializer address; the mutant that always returns address(0) breaks this for initializer addresses ≠ address(0).

For every nonzero address A used as msg.sender during initialize, the reference contract's owner() call (wrapped in a try/catch) always returns a non-zero address (it does not revert and returns the stored owner), whereas the mutant returns address(0) for some initializer addresses so a try/catch + equality to non-zero will fail for those inputs.

For any caller address X that invokes initialize on C, the reference returns owner() == X (nonzero if X nonzero); the mutant that hardcodes owner() to address(0) will cause owner() to differ from the initializer for some fuzzed initializer addresses.

For any caller address, the correct contract's owner() always returns the stored owner (the address set at initialize), whereas the mutant returns msg.sender so it will differ for callers other than the stored owner.

For any caller, the reference contract's owner() always returns the stored owner address (the one set at initialize), whereas the mutant incorrectly returns msg.sender so calling owner() from an address different than the stored owner yields a differing return value.

For any caller address A, the reference contract's owner() view always returns the initialized owner address (set during initialize), while the mutant returns msg.sender so invoking owner() from any caller A != initialized owner yields a differing result.

For every caller address A, after initialize(...) the reference contract's owner() view always returns the fixed initialized owner address (the deployer/prank used in initialize), while the mutant returns msg.sender so calling owner() from any A != initialized owner will produce a different return — thus there exists some caller A for which owner() differs.

After initialize(...) the contract's owner() always equals the originally-initialized owner address regardless of the caller; the mutant instead returns msg.sender, so calling owner() from any caller different from the initialized owner yields a differing return value.

For any stored owner value, C.owner() returns the exact stored owner address (no change in bits); the mutant that re-casts through uint160/uint256 may alter the returned address for some stored values, violating this identity.

For any stored owner value (any address written by initialize), owner() must return exactly that stored address; the mutant that re-casts via uint160/uint256 can change the returned address for some stored bit patterns, so there exists an input (the initialized owner address) for which mutant.owner() != original.owner().

For every address used to initialize C as owner, calling owner() returns exactly that same address; the mutant that re-casts the stored owner through extra uint160/uint256 conversions can change returned bits for certain owner values, so there exists an initialization owner that makes mutant.owner() != original.owner().

For any address used to initialize the contract as owner, the owner() getter must return exactly that stored owner address; the mutant's extra cast through uint160/uint256 can change the returned address for some owner values, so there exists an initialized owner address where mutant.owner() != original.owner().

For any address used to initialize C via initialize(), the owner() getter returns that exact stored owner address; the mutant that re-casts the stored owner through extra uint160/uint256 conversions can produce a different returned address for some initialized owner values, violating this equality.
